articles.title: Home Assistant makes integrations easier to find
articles.dek: Browse integrations by what they do, filter for local connections, and share the exact results.
body: The integration directory on Home Assistant’s website gains categories and subcategories that follow the things people want to connect, from heating to water heaters. A Local or Cloud filter helps narrow the choice, and search recognizes category names, small spelling mistakes and accented characters.

Categories and filters open in full-screen panels on phones. The selected category, search and filters stay in the address, so sharing a link or pressing Back preserves the view. Older category links redirect to their new homes.

Brand listings that rely on another integration follow its categories too: Somfy, for example, appears alongside the relevant Overkiz categories. The same categories are recorded across Home Assistant’s integrations, with support for custom integrations to supply them too.

Show virtual integrations in the categories of their supporting integration
Keep Featured out of the integration category counts
Add categories to all integration manifests
Accept categories in custom integration manifests

media.alt: Home Assistant integration directory with category navigation and filters

articles.title: ESPHome cameras connect to standard video players and recorders
articles.dek: A new stream works with VLC, go2rtc and Frigate without an ESPHome-specific connection.
body: ESPHome adds a standard video stream for cameras connected to an ESP32. The RTSP server sends Motion JPEG pictures to clients such as VLC, go2rtc and Frigate, giving makers another way to view or record their camera feed.

The server starts the camera stream when a viewer connects and stops it when viewers leave. A slow viewer drops a frame rather than holding up other consumers. It supports two connections by default and can restrict access to chosen IP addresses; the connection uses plain TCP, so it belongs on a trusted network.

pullRequests.title: [rtsp_server] Add an RTSP server that streams the esp32_camera picture
[rtsp_server] Document the RTSP server component

articles.title: Home Assistant maps LoRaWAN devices and their gateways
articles.dek: A new connectivity view brings connection lists, radio details and a gateway map together.
body: People managing LoRaWAN devices gain a dedicated overview in Home Assistant. The long-range wireless network’s devices can be grouped by connection, and a topology map shows the gateways receiving them, making the network easier to inspect in one place.

Device pages expose radio information, while unsupported devices still receive an information view. Setup links lead to the relevant connection’s management console. The accompanying backend supplies active connections, their devices and gateway reception information through administrator-only APIs.
The panel builds on Home Assistant’s shared LoRaWAN foundation. It distinguishes devices that Home Assistant cannot yet represent, rather than implying every device on the network is supported.

Expose LoRaWAN devices and connection metadata

media.alt: LoRaWAN gateway topology view in Home Assistant

articles.title: ESPHome gives scripts clear choices and a way to clean up
articles.dek: New branches choose the first matching action, while stopped scripts can run their own cleanup.
body: ESPHome scripts gain a choice action for selecting the first matching branch and an optional fallback when none matches. A new stop trigger also lets a script respond when it is interrupted, including when a restart-mode script starts again; it does not run after normal completion.

Clyde Stubbs supplies the script changes, with companion Device Builder work for editing each branch and preserving its conditions. The visual editor also stops turning an “any” condition into a requirement that every condition be true. Full editing of the new choices depends on the editor receiving the ESPHome 2026.11 schema.

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps YouTube Music sign-ins from quietly expiring
articles.dek: Automatic session renewal reduces repeated cookie replacement, with a small but important setup instruction.
body: Music Assistant preserves the sign-in updates sent back by YouTube Music instead of continuing to reuse an ageing copy. It also renews the session every ten minutes, reducing the need to paste fresh sign-in cookies when the saved session expires.

The setup guide adds a necessary step: copy the cookie from an incognito window, then close that window without signing out. Leaving it open lets the browser keep changing the same session. Existing saved settings keep their format, and a genuinely expired session still asks for fresh credentials.
Bautista Igarzabal makes his first contributions to Music Assistant’s server and documentation repositories with the paired changes.

articles.title: Piper brings Japanese speech to its native library
articles.dek: Apps using the C++ speech engine gain Japanese voice support, with a separate dictionary required.
body: Applications built on Piper’s native C++ library gain the ability to synthesize Japanese voices that previously produced silence. Ihor Shevchuk adds the text-to-pronunciation processing already present in Piper’s Python package, extending it to software that embeds the native engine.

Applications must supply the matching OpenJTalk pronunciation dictionary separately; it is not bundled with the library. A test on an Apple Silicon Mac produced speech with the Japanese Hi-Fi Captain voice. Applications still need to adopt this native-library support; it does not establish a Japanese voice release in Home Assistant.

pullRequests.title: feat: add OpenJTalk phonemization for Japanese voices

articles.title: ESPHome looks inside Pylontech batteries cell by cell
articles.dek: Individual voltage and temperature readings supplement the battery’s overall measurements.
body: ESPHome adds voltage and temperature readings for individual cells in Pylontech batteries. Owners can select the cells they want to monitor instead of relying only on the battery-wide figures.

The connection requests those details after its ordinary battery readings and can pause or resume cell polling from an automation. The extra requests and storage apply only to batteries configured with cell sensors.

[pylontech] Document the cell sensors and the set_cell_polling action

articles.title: ESPHome gives air-quality builders finer readings and calibration
articles.dek: SEN6x sensors gain particle counts, fault indicators and settings for their surroundings.
body: ESPHome expands its Sensirion SEN6x support with particle counts across five size ranges and diagnostic readings for problems such as a failing fan or measurement channel. The fault readings are checked even when an ordinary measurement fails, helping a maker distinguish a sensor fault from the air it is measuring.

Brandon Harvey also adds temperature compensation and a configurable warm-up period. CO₂-capable models gain self-calibration, altitude and air-pressure settings, including pressure supplied by another sensor. The hardware checks cover a SEN65 for particle readings and temperature settings; its lack of CO₂ sensing means those controls remain specific to the appropriate variants.

articles.title: Music Assistant protects desktop settings during troubleshooting
articles.dek: A rejected settings file stays intact, while diagnostic output hides recognized sign-in secrets.
body: Music Assistant’s desktop app stops replacing an unreadable settings file with defaults. It uses temporary defaults in memory, displays the file location and recovery instructions, and blocks saving until the file is repaired or removed and the app restarted.

David Bishop also removes recognized passwords, tokens and credentials embedded in addresses from the app’s logs and error diagnostics. Failed saves are reported and the affected controls return to their previous state, rather than suggesting the change succeeded.

articles.title: ESPHome reads Vevor weather stations over their local radio link
articles.dek: Temperature, rain, wind and light readings can join local automations.
body: ESPHome adds a receiver for Vevor 7-in-1 weather stations, bringing outdoor temperature, humidity, wind, rainfall, ultraviolet and light readings into a local device. It also reports the station’s low-battery flag.
The radio receiver can be shared with other supported protocols, and a station identifier filters out neighbouring stations. This is Bofr5555’s first contribution to ESPHome.

articles.title: ESPHome turns a compatible Xteink reader into an e-paper display
articles.dek: The X4 Pro variant with a UC8279 panel supports full and partial screen updates.
body: ESPHome adds the Xteink X4 Pro e-reader as a display target for makers building information screens. Support is specific to the model with a UC8279 controller; X4 Pro units with other panels need their own driver.

The implementation supports full refreshes and partial changes without rewriting the visible page from scratch. Related timing work cuts a tested X4 Pro partial update from roughly 980–1,000 milliseconds to 720–735 milliseconds, with one full refresh after every ten updates.

articles.title: HACS directs November upgrades to Home Assistant’s Marketplace
articles.dek: The installer stops at Home Assistant 2026.11, while a new guide explains which documentation applies.
body: HACS gives households preparing for Home Assistant 2026.11 a clearer route to the built-in Marketplace. Its installer refuses a separate HACS installation on that version and newer, including beta and development builds, and points to the matching Marketplace documentation.

Franck Nijhof’s new transition guide keeps the existing HACS instructions for Home Assistant 2026.10 and older. It explains the upgrade, directs publishers to the new contributor website, and tells users where Marketplace bugs and feature requests belong. Joakim Sørensen adds the version check to the installer.

articles.title: Home Assistant tracks Rituals refills with usable percentages
articles.dek: Numeric fill levels support low-fragrance automations, with a change needed for existing text comparisons.
body: Rituals Perfume Genie owners gain a numeric fill percentage that Home Assistant can graph and compare in automations. A separate Cartridge sensor reports whether a fragrance cartridge is inserted, rather than hiding that information in the perfume name.

Existing automations that compare fill levels with text such as “70-80%” need to compare against a number instead. A missing measurement becomes unknown; the perfume sensor also becomes unknown without a cartridge. On first- and second-generation diffusers, the percentage is estimated from the cartridge’s use counter within the range reported by Rituals.

articles.title: Music Assistant removes repeated clicks from phone playback
articles.dek: A timing correction stops interrupting the audio signal, including crackle on Bluetooth output.
body: Music Assistant’s phone player keeps the audio signal continuous while adjusting playback timing. A lost sample at the boundary between audio blocks caused repeated clicks—about forty a minute in the reported clock-drift case—and could become steady crackle over Bluetooth.
Andrii Mitnovych carries the audio through the same correction path even when its timing is already close enough. Deliberate gaps, such as inserted silence, still reset the correction.

articles.title: ESPHome sends Jarolift commands to the intended shutters
articles.dek: Correct group messages stop a command for one channel also addressing channel ten.
body: ESPHome adds the group message format used by Jarolift TDEF shutter controls. The earlier transmitter format could address channel ten unintentionally when sending a command intended for one of channels one through eight.

The new group setting supplies the extra channel bits used by Jarolift receivers and works with compatible 433 MHz transmitters, including a CC1101 radio. It also makes the received group value available to automations.

articles.title: ESPHome keeps nRF52 crash details until someone can read them
articles.dek: Makers can retrieve a stored crash report over USB after the device restarts.
body: ESPHome adds persistent crash reports for nRF52 devices. A crash saves debugging information in flash, and the next log reader receives it before it is erased, so a maker does not need to have a computer listening when the fault happens.

Tests on an nRF52840 dongle and an Adafruit ItsyBitsy recovered complete reports after opening the USB log port about a minute after the crash. Enabling or disabling the crash-report component on an existing over-the-air setup requires one USB flash because it changes the firmware storage layout.

articles.title: Home Assistant restores Live Activities while the iPhone app is closed
articles.dek: A local push can fall back to Apple’s delivery service when the app cannot start the activity.
body: Home Assistant’s iPhone app stops leaving a locally received Live Activity invisible until the app opens. The notification extension waits for the app to confirm that it displayed the activity, instead of acknowledging delivery immediately.

If the app is in the background or does not answer within two seconds, delivery falls back to Apple’s push-to-start service while the local push connection is registered again. This repairs a regression introduced by the recent local-push reconnection changes.
